title: Unlock ARIS: Run Reports from External Applications
description: Our discovery connects external applications to the power of ARIS report scripting. Run checks, automate updates and get results back, beyond the limits of the standard REST API.

content.html:
What if the limits of the standard ARIS REST API no longer defined the limits of your integration?

Your business application could ask ARIS to check processes, apply your business rules or prepare a document, then use the answer automatically. The work happens inside ARIS. The result comes back to the system that requested it.

At ArisTechnical, we uncovered and validated a way to make that connection: run ARIS reports from external applications, send them inputs and retrieve their results. This discovery opens a much wider range of ARIS capabilities to integration.

The standard API is only part of the story

A REST API is a way for applications to communicate. The standard ARIS API offers a defined set of operations. When your requirement goes beyond those operations, an otherwise promising integration can hit a wall.

ARIS has another source of power: report scripts. Despite their name, reports can do much more than produce a document. They can analyse processes, combine information, apply custom rules and change repository content.

Our breakthrough is connecting that power to applications outside ARIS, with a result they can use. The integration can request a tailored operation carried out by a report, extending what is possible beyond the standard API.

If an ARIS report can do it, your application can request it and get the result back.

Why getting the result back changes everything

Starting a task is only half of an integration. The application also needs to know what happened. Did the processes pass the checks? Which records changed? Is the document ready?

Returning an answer closes that loop. Your portal can display findings, a dashboard can show calculated values, and a workflow can continue based on the outcome. No one needs to open ARIS and run the report manually for each request.

Put more of ARIS to work

  • Bring process insights into your business tools. Request analysis shaped around your questions and return the findings directly to the application your team uses.
  • Automate repository work. Use report logic to validate inputs, apply business rules and make permitted updates, with confirmation sent back to the calling system.
  • Deliver documents on demand. Extend the integration to generate a file, store it in ARIS Document Storage and return a link for authorised retrieval.
  • Build on reports you already have. Suitable existing reports can be adapted for automated inputs and outputs, putting your investment in ARIS scripting to work across more systems.

These are starting points. The real opportunity is to define the ARIS operation your business needs, implement it in a suitable report and make it available through an API-driven workflow.

A discovery with a working proof of concept

We tested the complete round trip on ARIS 10.2025.10.0: an external application authenticated, started a prepared report with input parameters, followed its execution and retrieved structured results that it could read and verify.

That is the foundation we have demonstrated. Quality checks, repository updates and document delivery are examples of solutions that can be built on it, with a suitable report and integration design.

The scope follows what the ARIS Script API makes available to the report, together with the environment's permissions and licences. Each implementation must be checked against its ARIS version. This opens the potential of report scripting to REST-based integration; it does not remove the platform's own access rules.

For technical context, ARIS documents the distinction between its REST and Report APIs in the Repository API guide, and describes the broader capabilities of scripts in Use reports.

What would you connect if the API went further?

A process check inside your portal? An update triggered by another business system? A document delivered when your team needs it?

Tell us what should start the task, what ARIS should do and what your application needs back. ArisTechnical can assess the opportunity, develop a custom report or adapt an existing one, and build the connection around your workflow.

title: Call a REST API from an ARIS Report
description: A practical guide to calling REST APIs from ARIS reports with NetUtils: send GET and POST requests, handle JSON and configure timeouts.

content.html:
An ARIS report can fetch data from another system or send information to it over HTTP. This lets you enrich report output with external data, check repository content against another source or pass calculated results into a business workflow.

The ARIS Script API provides a built-in HTTP helper: Utilities.getNetUtils().doRestCall(...). Here is a small example you can adapt.

1. Fetch JSON with a GET request

Create a report in code view with Database context. The example uses no selected models and generates no output file. It calls JSONPlaceholder, a public test API that requires no credentials. The ARIS report execution server must be able to reach it.

What the code does

java.util.HashMap supplies the request headers. The "json" argument selects the response format for the Accept header; it does not parse the response.

doRestCall returns the response body as a string. String(...) converts it to a JavaScript string, and JSON.parse(...) creates the object used by the report. The final two arguments set connection and read timeouts in milliseconds; they are not a total execution deadline.

The report validates the fields it needs, then creates a result object containing:

Use the parsed values in further report processing or feed them into your report output logic.

2. Send JSON with a POST request

To send data, serialize the payload with JSON.stringify(...), set its Content-Type and pass it as the fifth argument. Use this self-contained example as an alternative to the GET report:

JSONPlaceholder simulates creation and returns a response containing an ID; it does not persist the new record. For a real integration, replace the URL and payload with your target API's contract.

Adapting this for your environment

For an authenticated API, add the required header to the same map, for example Authorization: Bearer <access token>. Obtain credentials through your approved configuration or secret management mechanism and keep them out of published report code and logs.

Confirm server connectivity, proxy requirements and trusted HTTPS certificates. Handle request failures and validate the API's error response contract before using returned data. Parsing JSON alone does not establish success. If you need access to the HTTP status as well as the body, consider the ARIS ConnectionService API. Avoid automatically repeating a POST that might already have been processed.

The method signature shown here was checked against the ARIS 10.0.27 Script API documentation. Confirm availability and behaviour in your installed version.
